$ go test  # used-fewer-a
    the lift import is used by ./b, and no package owns it, so its error is recorded nowhere.
        Own the lift in one of them: give it to hypercase.Own in place of hypercase.Use.
    the lift parse is used by ./b on the path testdata/export/ → import → parse, and ., which owns it, doesn't run it over testdata/export/, so no package writes its cells of that corpus's cases, which ./b's cells past it are built through.
        A package that uses a lift reaches it from each corpus by the path the lift's owner does: either . runs parse over testdata/export/ by that path, or ./b doesn't reach parse from testdata/export/. If one holds already, a registry is stale: run FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./..., which rewrites the registry of every package with tests.
    the lift resolve is used by ./b on the path testdata/export/ → import → parse → resolve, and ., which owns it, doesn't run it over testdata/export/, so no package writes its cells of that corpus's cases, which ./b's cells past it are built through.
        A package that uses a lift reaches it from each corpus by the path the lift's owner does: either . runs resolve over testdata/export/ by that path, or ./b doesn't reach resolve from testdata/export/. If one holds already, a registry is stale: run FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./..., which rewrites the registry of every package with tests.
--- FAIL: TestCorpus
    --- PASS: TestCorpus/script
    --- PASS: TestCorpus/checks
        --- PASS: TestCorpus/checks/paths
FAIL
[exit 1]
